request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"rethinkdb::devtools","name":"rethinkdb","one_liner":"Free, open-source distributed document database with real-time change feeds, seeded by YC in 2009, shut down in 2016 after failing to build a sustainable commercial business around an open-source core.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":4,"rationale":"Both target developers and distribute software that underpins cloud/infrastructure workflows. However, RethinkDB was free/open-source with no disclosed commercial monetization layer, while the new pitch is an explicit B2B SaaS with a hosted control plane — a meaningful structural difference, though the open-core tension is a shared risk."},"market":{"score":5,"rationale":"Both serve the developer/DevOps tooling market and compete for developer mindshare in infrastructure-adjacent categories. RethinkDB targeted app developers needing a real-time database; the pitch targets DevOps/platform engineers managing ephemeral preview environments. Adjacent but not identical market segments."},"gtm":{"score":6,"rationale":"Both rely heavily on developer adoption as the primary GTM motion — CLI-first distribution, open community, bottoms-up adoption before enterprise deals. RethinkDB used open-source community traction as its primary distribution channel, which mirrors a CLI-first developer tool strategy."},"stage_scale":{"score":5,"rationale":"RethinkDB reached Series A/B scale (YC-seeded, multi-year runway) before shutting down. The new pitch appears early-stage. Some overlap in the zero-to-one developer-adoption phase, but RethinkDB had 7 years of runway before failure, so scale context differs materially."}},"why_similar":"RethinkDB and the new pitch share the same primary buyer persona (developers), the same bottoms-up GTM instinct (CLI/tooling-first adoption), and the same core challenge: converting a free, developer-beloved product into a sustainable commercial business. Both operate in infrastructure-adjacent categories where technical excellence is necessary but insufficient for revenue. The open-source-to-paid-hosted tension RethinkDB never resolved is a live risk for any developer tool that ships a free CLI alongside a hosted tier.","where_diverged":"Three concrete divergences exist. First, monetization model: the new pitch is explicitly B2B SaaS with a hosted control plane (subscription or usage-based), whereas RethinkDB was priced at free with no commercial tier that succeeded — the new pitch has a revenue mechanism baked in from day one. Second, product category: RethinkDB was a general-purpose distributed database; the new pitch is a narrow DevOps workflow tool (ephemeral preview environments), a more bounded problem with clearer ROI for engineering teams. Third, era and ecosystem: the new pitch targets multi-cloud ephemeral environments, a category that did not exist at RethinkDB's founding (2009) and that now has established enterprise willingness-to-pay (e.g., Vercel, Railway precedents).","failure_causes":["inability to monetize a free open-source product","no sustainable commercial support or paid tier before runway exhausted","open-source gave away the primary value without capturing revenue","developer love did not convert to enterprise contracts at sufficient scale","product pivot timing (production-ready declared in 2015) was too late relative to burn","engineering team acqui-hired by Stripe, signaling talent retention pressure"],"lessons_for_input":["Price the hosted control plane from day one — never let the CLI be the only free path to full value without a clear upgrade trigger.","Define a concrete paid tier (seats, environment-hours, or concurrent previews) before launch so monetization is structural, not retrofitted.","Instrument CLI usage to identify which teams are power users and convert them to hosted tier via usage-based nudges before they self-host instead.","Avoid positioning the open-source CLI as the flagship product; make the hosted control plane the default happy path with the CLI as an on-ramp.","Set explicit revenue milestones tied to fundraising tranches — developer love without MRR growth will not sustain a multi-year runway."]}
